messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created (1781234567) — elevated p95 latency and memory pressure on inference-pool-7. Auto-scaler triggered. Alert: KV-cache used=96%, paging spikes observed.

maya: seeing huge latency cliffs on paged models, started ~09:12 UTC. Latency p95 jumped 4x, requests queued. Looks like block-manager is doing full rescans and thrashing eviction.

sam: oncall-ack. I'm on it. tagging runtime eng @kyler. Any recent deploys to block-manager or batching?

kyler: not a deploy in last 2h. We rolled a config change to continuous-batching defaults last week; could be interaction with paged kv blocksize heuristics. Pulling logs now.

maya: example log snippet (from host gpu-13):
```
[09:12:03] block_manager: eviction_scan took=1273ms scanned=18432 live_blocks=1032
[09:12:03] kv_cache: page_faults=4321 io_wait_ms=5123 cache_size_bytes=12456832000
[09:12:03] batching: active_batches=48 avg_latency_ms=920
```

alice: that eviction_scan time is huge. Could be metadata walk is O(n) and we hit worst-case with many small blocks. Are block_size tunables exposed?

kyler: yes — block_size_bytes and eviction_policy (LRU/size_based). Current prod defaults: block_size_bytes=65536 (64KB), eviction_policy=LRU. Small blocks + large working set -> massive metadata overhead.

sam: mitigation plan options: 1) temporarily increase block_size to reduce #blocks and metadata ops 2) switch eviction_policy to size_based to avoid scanning 3) throttle continuous batching concurrency to reduce memory pressure 4) roll back recent batching param changes. Thoughts?

maya: customer impact: several enterprise customers on dedicated pools seeing 5-10s errors/timeouts. CS escalation open (lia-cs). Need status update for them in 20m.

lia-cs: confirmed multiple customer reports. One high-value customer saw generator timeouts and fallback to older endpoint. They asked for ETA.

kyler: I'm in favor of a fast config hotpatch: increase block_size to 256KB and flip eviction_policy to size_based. That should reduce metadata entries ~4x and avoid full scans. Low-risk config change if we scope to pool inference-pool-7 first.

sam: agree. Also reduce continuous_batch_max_concurrent from 64->24 to give breathing room. We'll do canary on 2 hosts, monitor for 10m, then rollout.

maya: do we have a one-liner to apply via fleetctl?

kyler: yes — patch below. Deploying via runtime-config service:
```bash
fleetctl apply --pool inference-pool-7 --patch '{"block_manager.block_size_bytes":262144,"block_manager.eviction_policy":"size_based","batching.continuous_batch_max_concurrent":24}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy started by kyler (1781235870). Jobs: config-patch -> canary group (gpu-13,gpu-42).

kyler: canary applied to gpu-13,gpu-42. Watching metrics.

maya: initial signs: canary hosts memory usage dropped ~30%, eviction_scan times down to ~120ms. p95 latency on canary traffic down ~60%.

sam: good. Start staggered rollout to remaining hosts, 10% increments every 3 minutes with health checks. If error rate > 2% halt.

deploy-bot: Rollout 10% -> 30% (1781236234).

alice: monitoring note: we should also add a short-term guard to avoid metadata walk while eviction_scan > 200ms — fast-fail to size_based path. I'll file follow-up.

kyler: rolling to 100% now.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete (1781236650).

maya: post-rollout metrics: overall p95 down to baseline+10%, cache memory stable at 68%. No new paging spikes in 18m.

lia-cs: passing update to affected customers: we applied a config hotpatch to reduce metadata churn and throttle batching. Expecting normal behavior. Customers confirmed decreased errors.

sam: incident summary for postmortem: root cause likely interaction between small block_size + continuous_batching increases that expanded working set and triggered O(n) metadata scans in block_manager -> eviction_scan thrash -> paging. Mitigation: hotpatch increased block_size and changed eviction_policy + reduced batching concurrency.

alice: next steps (assigned): kyler — implement size-based eviction fast-path and avoid global scans; maya — prepare eval harness to replay large working sets; alice — add a runtime guard/alert for eviction_scan latency; sam — include config change in runbook.

kyler: will also add a migration script to gradually coalesce small blocks for models pinned at high traffic.

maya: preparing blameless postmortem draft. Lia, please collect impacted customer list for severity classification.

lia-cs: collecting now, will attach list to the postmortem doc.

sam: handing off to night oncall @kyler_night at 18:00 UTC. Night oncall, please watch eviction_scan > 200ms or p95>1.5x baseline and reopen incident if regressions.

kyler: ack takeover. Leaving a short checklist in the incident thread.

oncall-bot: Incident (1781234567) status: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff complete to kyler_night.

maya: thanks everyone. Will finalize postmortem and link here. :white_check_mark:
